coordinates.origin: Whole animal centered, meters, +Z up; no slab/pedestal

concept.reason: Primary published full-body reconstruction and actual calibrated scale photographs available; additional concept image would not resolve missing soft tissue evidence.

scope: Original608 whole living porolepiform with broad flattened predatory head and rounded overlapping scales, not a scale-only or fossil-slab study.
evidence_resolution: Original group-only hold addressed by named taxon-specific2020 original paper Fig1 genus reconstruction, H.jarviki squamation and specimen-scale evidence; exact species soft anatomy is not established.
reference_specimens: H. jarviki squamation, Mondejar-Fernandez & Meunier2020 Fig1B after Orvig1957
NBMG13038 Holoptychius sp., Miller & Brazeau2007, genus-level scale comparison only
MNHN URSS5075 and MB.f1994.1,2020 Fig1C-F scale comparison only

scale.status: Illustrative whole-animal size, not a measured length of any pictured specimen. Fossil scales in primary2020Fig1 are calibrated by10mm bars;2007 NBMG13038 scales about2cm diameter.
scale.uncertainty: Do not claim reconstructed body length measured from isolated scales. Total size, cross-section and palette are artistic assumptions; anatomical proportions follow published genus reconstruction.

material_policy: Muted slate/olive body with slightly lighter belly and subtle darker scale ridges, opaque low-poly palette. No copyrighted reference pixels or fossil texture.
diagnostic_targets: Broad blunt flattened head, wide predatory mouth and lateral eyes, not a tall narrow cone head.
Stocky elongated trunk clad in rounded overlapping scale fields. Scales must be visibly overlapping rounded plates, not diamonds, shark skin, or random spheres.
Exposed flank scales carry a few simplified posteriorly oriented ridges; upper and side scale sculpture differs from more tuberculate ventral region. No thousands of separate grains.
Pectoral paired fleshy lobed fins large near shoulder; smaller paired pelvic fins well posterior.
Two separated dorsals crowded into posterior body, second larger; a discrete posterior anal fin, and asymmetrical tapering caudal fin following2020Fig1A.

Head and scale combination is essential. Do not merely recolor Dipterus: no lungfish toothplates, no reusing its narrow smooth body. Mouth may be slightly parted with restrained pointed teeth, not giant external saber fangs.
uncertainties: Published Fig1A is genus reconstruction after Jarvik1980, not a photograph of an intact specimen.
H.jarviki supplies scale pattern, while other labeled species specimens corroborate genus scales only. Do not claim one exact individual or silent mixed-species scan.
Color, soft lip form, body thickness and pose are original reconstruction choices.
Eye and tooth fine counts not established, avoid numerical anatomy claims.
acceptance_checklist: Original full living body scope preserved, no scale tile/slab substitute.
Broad flattened head and clear round imbricated scale silhouette both visible in default4 views.
Posterior dorsal arrangement/paired fleshy fins/tail agree with primary reconstruction.
Rounded scale relief follows body without spikes, gaps to body or excessive geometry.
Two self-contained rebuilds and exact-GLB default4 views; independent review separate.
